claims: Palm Sunday is celebrated on the Sunday before Easter.
Palm Sunday commemorates Jesus's humble entry into Jerusalem on a donkey.
Palm Sunday marks the start of Holy Week.
According to the Gospels, Jesus arrived in Jerusalem amid great anticipation following the raising of Lazarus, as described by Bible Study Tools.
Jesus purposefully chose to ride a young donkey (or colt) rather than a warhorse.
Jesus riding a young donkey fulfilled Zechariah's prophecy.
GotQuestions.org and YouTube state that Jesus's donkey ride signaled that he was a king coming in peace, not through force.
People celebrated Jesus's arrival by spreading their cloaks and palm branches on the road.
People shouted "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!".
Palm branches are recognized as a sign of victory and honor, according to Baylor Magazine and Trinity Church.
Palm Sunday is called "Palm Sunday of the Lord's Passion".
In some traditions, palm branches are taken home to be placed behind crucifixes or kept until the next Lent when they are burned to make ashes.
Wikipedia and The Seattle Times describe church members walking in public processions through streets in other regions.
Easter's date changes based on the lunar calendar.
Palm Sunday typically falls between March 22 and April 25, according to Austin American-Statesman and Christianity.com.
